_doc: Rules of the C++ extractor (keys: see ts_generic.rules_of). static = private; virtual = dispatch (flag abstract: base.m reaches the overrides, link.py); override/final = override. `static` is private only on a function of a file or namespace (defs.scm), never on a class member; an anonymous namespace is private. Access sections (`private:`) are not read: every member is public, a `static` member too (documented gap: closed-world verdicts are not affected, library mode keeps every member as API). A function under `template<>` has no @mod (public). strip_angles: `Foo<T>::get` is Foo.get (a template member written out of the class). protocol: an operator (out of class: `Foo::operator==` is never called by name) and the members the language calls by convention (range-for begin/end, coroutine promise members, ADL swap/to_json) are alive with their class; a free function of such a name is a root (annotation.adl). A weak, section, interrupt, alias or naked function is a link-time or hardware entry (annotation.c-attribute); the entry points of a loader (DllMain, JNI_OnLoad, Java_*, PyInit_*) are roots (main). annotation.cpp-hook: a member that a framework or a registry calls by name or by a string (a URI) and nothing in the tree calls: the singleton factory `instance()`, the route registration `getRoutes()` that hands `this` to a router, the entry `execute()` of a command; soft roots, the list is data (a class built by such a factory is reached from outside the tree).
